Subject: Audit logging capabilities & SOC 2 — follow-up

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation today — really appreciate the level of detail on your compliance needs. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- What we discussed: audit logging (admin activity, API request/response logging), retention/export options, immutability requirements, and SOC 2 status.
- Redwood status: SOC 2 Type II attestation is in process; we expect a final report early Q1 2027. Attached is our most recent SOC 2 attestation snapshot and a short Audit Logging spec doc for your review.
- Audit logging details (high level):
  - Admin activity logs: user id, actor email, action, timestamp, resource, IP address.
  - API logs: request and response metadata, headers, truncated payloads (payloads are masked by default for PII), latency and error codes.
  - Retention: default 90 days; configurable up to 365 days for Enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments.
  - Export: logs can be exported to S3/BigQuery or downloaded as compressed CSVs. Exports are signed and time-stamped for auditability.
  - Immutability: we provide write-once export bundles and signed hashes for long-term retention; for strict immutability needs we recommend Dedicated/Private with object-lock configured on the receiving storage.

Next steps (action owners):
- Marissa (me): share SOC2_Attestation.pdf and Audit_Logging_Specs.pdf (attached) — done.
- Acme: send the completed vendor security questionnaire (I saw you had one on the call).
- Soojin (copied): will follow up with a short tech note on field-level masking and retention policy options, plus a sample S3 export manifest.
- Neha (copied): will start the vendor questionnaire kickoff and share the Redwood contact for any security evidence requests.

Happy to jump on another call if you want to walk through the spec line-by-line. Proposed: 30-min technical deep dive with Soojin and Dev (solutions/dev) — please let us know availability.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah —

Quick answers below and we'll cover the rest in the tech session.

1) Request/response bodies: Redwood does not store full request/response bodies by default for managed hosted plans — payloads are truncated to the first X KB and sensitive fields are masked using our PII detection regexes. For Dedicated/Private deployments, you can opt into full payload logging, but we recommend field-level masking via configuration.

2) Exports: We support push to customer S3 (preferred) using short-lived AWS STS credentials we generate per-export and rotate. We also support scheduled exports to BigQuery via a service account, or on-demand downloads (compressed CSV). Transfer is authenticated via temporary credentials and the export bundles are signed server-side.

3) Immutability: Every export bundle includes a signed SHA256 manifest with timestamps. For long-term immutability we recommend configuring object-lock/retention on the target storage. We can include a notarized hash if you need third-party verification.

I'll have Soojin drop a short tech note (1-2 pages) with: sample S3 manifest, example log fields, retention config, and recommended masking rules. Dev will prepare a quick demo script for how exports are triggered via API.

Proposed times for a 30-min deep dive: Tue 2026-11-16 16:00 PT or Wed 2026-11-17 11:00 PT — let me know which works.

Also, Neha will start the vendor questionnaire kickoff and can request any additional evidence from our security ops team.

Thanks — talk soon.

Marissa
